mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has climbed monotonically across the four weekly means (-1.6, -0.4, -0.1, +0.3) and crossed zero in the final week; this within-regime drift persists, so the next 28-day mean exceeds the last 28-day mean of -0.45 because the recovery slope has not yet flattened.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased in each of the last four weekly means and turned positive at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the last 28-day mean of -0.45, rejecting continuation of the upward drift.

mechanism_narrative: Time-at-home is being drawn down: RESIDENTIAL fell from 4.0 to 3.7 while retail rose, so each further 0.3-point drop in the RESIDENTIAL four-week mean below 3.8 releases discretionary out-of-home trips that convert into RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 4.0 at t-3w to 3.7 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC rose
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 3.8 and RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is lower than its level at the week the threshold was crossed.

mechanism_narrative: When the WORKPLACES weekly mean exceeds +4.5, office occupancy is high enough to regenerate weekday lunchtime and after-work retail footfall; with TRANSIT already at 0.6 and not degrading, commuters retain the means to reach shops, and RETAIL_REC rises within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES peaked at 4.7 at t-2w and held 4.3 at t-0w; TRANSIT held 0.6
failure_condition: After WORKPLACES prints above +4.5 in a weekly mean, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the 14-day mean ending at the crossing week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT at 0.6 and WORKPLACES at 4.3 jointly encode a restored commute-plus-errand routine: only the interaction of both series sitting at or above baseline multiplies weekday retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC climbs over four weeks while either series alone would leave it flat.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean >= 0.0 and WORKPLACES weekly mean >= 4.0 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES sat at or above baseline in every week t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where both TRANSIT >= 0.0 and WORKPLACES >= 4.0, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is no higher than in weeks where only one of the two conditions holds.

mechanism_narrative: Late-autumn weather suppression is easing: PARKS improved in three of four weeks (-10.6 to -6.7). A PARKS weekly mean crossing above -7.0 marks that outdoor-avoidance is fading, and within one week the same release of pent-up demand appears in indoor retail-and-recreation venues.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -10.6 at t-3w to -6.7 at t-0w, its highest of the four weeks
failure_condition: In the seven days after PARKS exceeds -7.0, the weekly mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the weekly mean recorded in the week of the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is pinned on a 42.9-44.4 plateau, roughly 43 points above baseline; that persistence means a fixed share of household time and spend is still routed to at-home provisioning, capping discretionary reallocation and pulling the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean below the last 28-day mean of -0.45.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM four-week mean stays at or above 43.0
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM never left the 42.9-44.4 band across all four weeks
failure_condition: With GROCERY_PHARM at or above 43.0 for two consecutive weeks, the following 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds its 14-day mean at the start of that window.

mechanism_narrative: Transit normalization has stalled: TRANSIT has been flat at 0.1-0.7 across all four weeks while retail rose. Because discretionary trips requiring a transit leg need TRANSIT above +2.0 to widen catchment, the retail gain is capped and mean-reverts below -0.45 over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT varied only between -0.1 and 0.7 over the four weeks while RETAIL_REC rose 1.9 points
regime_hint: stalled transit recovery under residual capacity limits
failure_condition: With TRANSIT below +2.0 throughout, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the last 28-day mean of -0.45.

mechanism_narrative: Under a pre-holiday November ramp with no new retail capacity restrictions, gift and indoor-recreation spending accelerates on top of the existing drift; with GROCERY_PHARM stable near 43 the grocery channel is not draining budget, so the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean exceeds the last 28-day mean.
candidate_trigger: no new retail or workplace capacity restrictions announced during the 28-day window
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC reached +0.3 at t-0w while GROCERY_PHARM stayed flat near 43
regime_hint: pre-holiday November ramp with no new restrictions
failure_condition: In a restriction-free late-November window, the following 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC fails to exceed the last 28-day mean of -0.45.
